analysis.title: US Market Intelligence - Afternoon Briefing - Oct 6
key_insights: Oct 6 close: SPX +0.6%, NDX +0.5%, RTY -0.6%. SPX finished near a record high and 67% of SPX stocks rose. 2y and 10y Treasury yields fell 2bp and 3bp, helped by lower European yields and lower oil.
AI baskets and tech led, driven by MRVL's bullish Investor Day guidance (stock +6%). Airlines, Housing and Retail also outperformed in a broad recovery of reopening and rate-linked baskets.
Europe closed higher, led by Italy. France 2y and 10y yields fell 10bp and 11bp on Le Pen's promised cost savings, weak industrial production data and lower Brent earlier in the day.

Oil was weak in the morning on rebounding Hormuz exports under a major US military commitment and Yemeni government forces seizing a strategic strait from the Houthis. It reversed to finish 50-70bp higher, with Brent at $100.63. The desk saw no clear driver for the afternoon rebound.

Commodity positioning: open interest across tracked commodity markets fell 4% WoW (-$80B) to $1.9T as of Oct 2, mostly energy (-$35B, with $32B of net contract-based outflows around month-end expiries) and metals (-$34B). Net investor positioning in global commodity futures fell 11% WoW to $238B.

ETF desk (Rogerson) sees risk-on demand in thematic plays. Buyers of cybersecurity (CIBR) and global megacap (IOO), and heavy real-money demand for AI pure plays, which the desk is meeting by creating AIS, a Global AI Supercycle ETF. An issuer model rebalance is upweighting a defensive call-overwriting income strategy (BALI), with multiple blocks expected. International flow is quiet with China out for Golden Week, and recent supply is in Japan (EWJ, FLJP).

Financials desk (O'Dwyer) calls the tape constructive, with Financials acting as a catch-up and broadening trade. Large-cap banks remain oversold. He prefers MS and sees GS interest picking up below $900. Trading revenue growth looks more durable at best-in-class firms, but aggregate growth may decelerate as comps toughen. The key earnings watch is whether beats come from financing and client activity or from macro/FICC event volatility.

O'Dwyer pushes back on the idea that differentiated research is commoditized by AI, citing the Wolfe and Citadel Securities JV. He argues scale matters at an increasing rate and will drive different growth outcomes across firms.
Payments may be bottoming. SHOP is flagged as a high-quality AI/agentic commerce beneficiary, with upside tied to Catalog, Shop Pay and sustained high-20s growth.

MRVL raised its F28 revenue outlook to $20B, led by connectivity, with $18B from Data Center. That reaches the F29 target a year early, against a prior $16.1B (Harlan). The F31 (C30) guide has Data Center revenue at a +55%-70% CAGR ($67.5B-$87.5B) and total revenue of $70B-$90B.

MRVL reaction is a strong bull/bear debate. Bulls say the guide cleared the bar and leaves room versus optimistic buy-side expectations ("tracking toward $30 EPS"). Bears question giving credit to MRVL's C30 target given its poor track record, note NVDA is on 2x C30, and are unsure about margins (operating margins seem to be 40%-45%). People are also asking why ALAB is up more than CRDO.

Tech desk (Heavey) sees AI infrastructure names leading on MRVL, M Science data showing LLM software SMB billings and token usage accelerating, and re-grossing as crude and rates pull back. Security software keeps grinding higher. The desk is seeing additions to optical and semis from long-only and hedge fund accounts, plus covering in the tax-loss candidate trade.

Consumer desk (Murphy) reports crude near one-month lows (~$87) as Yemeni forces recaptured the coast around Bab el-Mandeb, and the Treasury curve breaking its steepening trend. Yesterday's consumer flows lacked the broadening investors want: little Discretionary demand, squeeze-like moves in BBWI and ANF, flat-to-down housing, cruise and airlines, and sharp restaurant underperformance in CMG and EAT.

Food producers face refinancing risk in a higher-rate environment, with debt above target and high dividend payout ratios limiting paydown. CPB, POST, GIS, BRBR and HRL face the greatest net-income headwinds if debt is refinanced at current rates. HRL is the only one with a significant portion (44%) due by end of 2028. The focus follows CPB's 8.5% debt issuance last week.

JPM Market Intel returned to a Tactically Bullish view, citing improving macro fundamentals, consumer strength, earnings expectations, stabilizing yields and supportive technicals. October rate-hike expectations fell from 64% to 22% and the 2Y moved from 4.85% to 4.82%. The market prices roughly 1 hike in 2026 and 2 in 2027.

Broadening of the rally likely requires yields to hold or fall. This week's ISM-Services Prices Paid, which tends to lead CPI by 2-3 months, and next week's CPI and PPI are the key rate catalysts. Barring an unexpected decline in inflation or inflation expectations, Tech should remain the leader.

Monetization Menu (unchanged from Sep 28): Tech as a core long, no longer paired with an RTY short because of squeeze risk from lower oil and yields, so a derivative expression is preferred for the squeeze. Semis and Mag 7 may outperform the Tech tape, software is a non-consensus bullish play, and ex-AI the desk favors Banks. Rate-sensitive sectors (Real Estate, Telecom, Utilities) may squeeze but likely lag the SPX.

The biggest upside catalyst named is a US/Iran deal, which would squeeze EU and RTY higher. The COVID Reopening theme (Airlines, Autos, Cruise Lines, Discretionary, Hotels) is another area of interest, preferably played through options.

Calendar: FOMC minutes Oct 7 at 2pm ET, CPI Oct 14, Retail Sales Oct 15, Fed Oct 28, PCE Oct 29. Earnings: APLD Oct 7, PEP Oct 8, DAL Oct 9. Political: US midterms Nov 3, trade truce dates around Nov 1 and Jan 20 2027, funding deadline Dec 11.

F31 Data Center revenue guided to a +55%-70% CAGR ($67.5B-$87.5B) and F31 total revenue to $70B-$90B ($80B midpoint). Operating margins seem to be 40%-45% per buy-side chatter. These are company targets, not reported results.
Earnings season kicks off this week with DAL and PEP. Calendar: LW, STZ, AEHR, BRUN and NEOG on Oct 6, APLD Oct 7, PEP Oct 8, DAL Oct 9.

Aggregate expectations (quoted from last week's JPM view): 26Q2 earnings growth printed +52% and the market sees ~29% for 26Q3, which may prove light as all 11 sectors are expected to show positive revenue and EPS growth.

Bank earnings: large-cap banks look healthier into earnings. Trading revenue growth looks more durable at best-in-class firms, while aggregate growth may decelerate as comps toughen. The key is whether beats come from financing and client activity or from macro/FICC event volatility.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Still elevated, so the report says the macro fundamental backdrop remains strong. The Prices Paid sub-index tends to lead CPI by 2-3 months.
Labor data was weaker than expected last Friday, but the 3-month average is stable and initial claims fell. JPM does not read the higher unemployment rate as a concern.
Payroll gains near 51k sit at or just above breakeven, which supports the case that the labor market is not showing distress.
Lower hike odds helped stabilize the front end of the curve and reduce bond volatility, which is typically supportive for long-duration growth.
